create.name: Tenshin Reb Anderson
create.bio:
Tenshin Reb Anderson is a Soto Zen teacher in the line of Shunryu Suzuki Roshi. Born in Mississippi in 1943 and raised in Minnesota, he gave up graduate work in mathematics and psychology in 1967 to train with Suzuki Roshi in San Francisco, was ordained a priest by him in 1970, and later received Dharma transmission. He went on to serve as abbot of San Francisco Zen Center and, over more than fifty years, lived and taught at its Green Gulch Farm in Marin County, leading long practice periods there and at Tassajara and training many priests and lay students.

Having left residence at Green Gulch, he now teaches from No Abode Hermitage in Mill Valley, California, where he holds monthly one-day sittings of zazen, walking meditation, work and two talks, and gives Dharma talks online; he also leads retreats and sesshin as a guest of sanghas in the United States and Europe. His books include Warm Smiles from Cold Mountains and Being Upright. His YouTube channel, active since 2013, carries his recent talks on zazen, bodhisattva practice and the Flower Adornment Scripture.
